status_note: A bug in the documentation. Reproduces on Polars 2.1.0 (Python, macOS arm64), both engines; the sentence is unchanged on main (35a2cb73, 2026-11-04). No matching issue found on pola-rs/polars (2026-11-04).
summary: The documentation of `list.get` (https://docs.pola.rs/api/python/stable/reference/expressions/api/polars.Expr.list.get.html, py-polars/src/polars/expr/list.py#L603-L624 at py-2.1.0) says "So index `0` would return the first item of every sublist and index `-1` would return the last item of every sublist if an index is out of bounds, it will return a `None`." The same sentence is in `Series.list.get` (series/list.py#L434), `Expr.arr.get` (expr/array.py#L822) and `Series.arr.get` (series/array.py#L613).

The same docstring's `null_on_oob` says "False -> raise an error", and its default is `False`: an out-of-range index raises `ComputeError: get index is out of bounds` (crates/polars-ops/src/chunked_array/list/namespace.rs#L320-L338, whose Rust doc comment at L320-L323 has the same stale sentence). The `arr` variants were not probed; their signature has the same default (expr/array.py#L816).
repro:
import polars as pl
pl.LazyFrame({"l": [[1], []]}).select(pl.col("l").list.get(0)).collect()
# ComputeError: get index is out of bounds
pl.LazyFrame({"l": [[1], []]}).select(pl.col("l").list.get(0, null_on_oob=True)).collect().rows()
# [(1,), (None,)]
handling: Nothing to work around: sverify follows the engine's behaviour, which the facts record. The fix is in Polars's documentation. Suggested fix: drop the sentence, or say "if an index is out of bounds, it raises, or returns `None` with `null_on_oob=True`".
found_by: the Polars characterization reverse pass (2026-11-04): the docstrings and user guide at py-2.1.0 checked against each open fact

checked.note: Repro on both engines (POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64). Main at 35a2cb73: expr/list.py#L616 still says "it will return a `None`". Duplicate search for "list.get out of bounds docs None" and "list.get null_on_oob docstring": no matching issue.
